(p-4561) Surah al-Furqan

The majority of scholars hold that it is Meccan. It is related from al-Dahhak that it is Medinan. It is related from some scholars that it is Meccan except for three verses, from "And those who do not invoke" to "merciful."

Al-Mahayimi said: It was named al-Furqan (the Criterion) because it contains the manifestation of the abundant goods of the Truth through the Furqan, which is the distinction between truth and falsehood. The more evident view is that it is named for the meanings of furqan mentioned in it, which the word is broad enough to encompass, and not only for what he mentioned. Its verses number seventy-seven.

(p-4562) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Discussion on the interpretation of the words of the Exalted:

[1] ﴿Blessed is He who sent down the Criterion upon His servant, that he may be a warner to the worlds.﴾

﴿Blessed is He who sent down the Criterion upon His servant, that he may be a warner to the worlds.﴾ Allah Exalted praises His noble Self and extols it for what He sent down of the Criterion, as He said: ﴿Praise be to Allah, who has sent down to His servant the Book and has not made therein any deviance﴾ [al-Kahf: 1] ﴿an upright [Book] to warn of severe punishment from Him and to give good tidings to the believers who do righteous deeds﴾ [al-Kahf: 2].

Al-Zamakhshari said: "Barakah" (blessing) is abundance and increase of good. From it: ﴿Blessed is Allah﴾ [al-A'raf: 54], and in it there are two meanings: His good has increased and multiplied, or He has exceeded everything and is exalted above it in His attributes and actions. And "al-Furqan" is a verbal noun from "faraqa bayna al-shay'ayn," when the two are separated. The Qur'an was named by it because it separates truth from falsehood, or because it was not sent down all at once, but divided, with some of it separated from other parts in its revelation.

Do you not see His saying: ﴿And a Qur'an We have divided, that you might recite it to the people at intervals, and We have sent it down in stages﴾ [al-Isra': 106]. End of quote.

Al-Nasir said: The more evident meaning here is the second. Because in the course of the surah, after the verse: ﴿And those who disbelieve say, "Why was the Qur'an not sent down to him all at once?"﴾ [al-Furqan: 32], Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Thus﴾ [al-Furqan: 32], meaning: We sent it down in parts in this manner, ﴿that We may strengthen your heart thereby﴾ [al-Furqan: 32]. So its description as al-Furqan at the beginning of the surah, and Allah knows best, serves as an introduction and preparation for what follows. End of quote.

Abu al-Su'ud said: His (ﷺ) being addressed with this title is for his honour, and to signal that he is at the highest rank of servanthood, and to alert that the Messenger is only a servant of the One who sent him, refuting the Christians. The pronoun in "li-yakun" refers either to the servant or to the Furqan. "Nadhir" is an adjective in the sense of "mundhir" (warner), or a verbal noun in the sense of "indhar" (warning), like "nukr" for emphasis.

The discussion of His saying, may He be exalted:

[2] ﴿He to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, who has not taken a son, and who has no partner in the dominion, and who created everything and determined it with precise measure.﴾

﴿He to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, who has not taken a son, and who has no partner in the dominion, and who created everything and determined it with precise measure.﴾ That is: He brought it into being in a manner in which measure and proportion are observed for what is intended from it, such as the creation of man for perception, understanding, reflection, management, deriving the various crafts, and pursuing beneficial works. Likewise every animal and inanimate thing was created in its determined form, in exemplary wisdom and arrangement for some matter, its benefit corresponding to what was decreed for it, without deviating from it.

Since this includes the affirmation of monotheism (tawhid) and prophethood (nubuwwah), He followed it with the proof for both and the refutation of those who oppose them, with His saying, glorified is He:

The commentary on His saying, exalted is He:

﴿And they have taken besides Him gods that create nothing while they are created, and possess not for themselves any harm or benefit, and possess not death or life or resurrection.﴾

﴿And they have taken besides Him gods that create nothing while they are created, and possess not for themselves any harm or benefit, and possess not death or life or resurrection.﴾ That is: they do not possess the averting of harm, nor the bringing of benefit, nor the causing of anyone's death and his giving of life at first, nor his raising again a second time. Whoever is like this is far removed from divinity (al-uluhiyya), since he is devoid of its requirements and characterized by what contradicts it. In this there is an admonition that the god (ilah) must be able to resurrect and to repay. This is what al-Qadi (al-Baydawi) conveyed.

(p-4564) Al-Shihab (al-Khafaji) said: He placed death first because of its relation to the harm mentioned before it. Death and life are explained as causing death, giving life, and raising up (al-inshar). This is either as a clarification of the sense that results, since the Angel of Death has the power to cause death, or as an indication that they carry the meaning of acts, as in His saying: ﴿And Allah has caused you to grow from the earth as a growth.﴾ [Nuh: 17]

**The interpretation of His saying, may He be exalted:**

[4–5] ﴿And those who disbelieve say, "This is nothing but a falsehood he has invented, and other people have helped him with it." Indeed, they have produced injustice and falsehood.﴾ ﴿And they say, "Tales of the ancients, which he has had written down, and they are dictated to him morning and evening."﴾ [al-Furqan: 5]

﴿And those who disbelieve say, "This is nothing but a falsehood he has invented, and other people have helped him with it. Indeed, they have produced injustice"﴾, meaning: by making truth into falsehood and by making the one who is innocent of assistance into one who assists. ﴿And falsehood﴾, meaning: baseless, having no truthfulness to it, while they themselves know from their own selves that it is false and a slander. ﴿And they say, "Tales of the ancients, which he has had written down"﴾ [al-Furqan: 5], meaning: what they have inscribed. He wrote them for himself and took them. ﴿They are dictated to him﴾ [al-Furqan: 5], meaning: they are cast upon him so that he may memorize them. ﴿Morning and evening﴾ [al-Furqan: 5], meaning: continually.

Ibn Kathir said: This speech, because of its absurdity, its lying, and its slander on their part, is known to everyone to be false. It is known by necessity that Muhammad (ﷺ), the Messenger of Allah, did not engage in any writing, neither at the beginning of his life nor at its end. He grew up among them from his earliest birth until Allah sent him, about forty years, and they knew his comings and goings, his truthfulness, his righteousness, his purity, and his trustworthiness, and his distance from lying, immorality, and all the other base characteristics. To the extent that they used to call him, in his youth and until he was sent, "al-Amin" (the Trustworthy), because of what they knew of his truthfulness and righteousness. When Allah honored him with what He honored him with, they set enmity against him and accused him with these statements, of which every sensible person knows his innocence. They were bewildered as to what to accuse him of. At one time, out of their falsehood, they would say, "He is a sorcerer." At another time they would say, "He is a poet." At another time they would say, "He is a madman." At another time they would say, "He is a liar." Allah, may He be exalted, said: ﴿See how they coin comparisons for you, so they have gone astray and cannot find a way﴾ [al-Furqan: 9]. And Allah, may He be exalted, said, in answer to what they fabricated here,

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[6] ﴿Say: "It was sent down by the One who knows the secret in the heavens and the earth. Indeed, He is ever Forgiving and Merciful."﴾

﴿Say: "It was sent down by the One who knows the secret in the heavens and the earth"﴾ — i.e., the hidden [secret] within them. This is an indication of His knowledge, exalted is He, of their condition, all the more so. From its requirement is His mercy toward them by sending it down, because of the increase in their need and the poverty of those like them to being brought out of the darknesses by His lights. Within it is also a warning to them that what they conceal of plotting against the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, along with what they fabricate and invent, is not hidden from His knowledge. So He will requite them for it by the vanishing of their falsehood and the erasure of their trace, and the elevation of His truth and the manifestation of His affair. ﴿Indeed, He is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾ is a causal explanation of what is witnessed of the delay of their punishment, despite their deserving it. That is: He gives respite and does not hasten, because of His forgiveness and mercy. Or the two attributes are a metaphor for the completeness of His power to take vengeance upon them, for forgiveness is only attributed to one who is able. This is what is derived from al-Kashshaf (al-Kashshaf, the tafsir of al-Zamakhshari) and those who followed it, in clarifying its correspondence with what precedes it.

Ibn Kathir said: His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿Indeed, He is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾ is a call to them to repentance and turning back [to Him], and an informing of them that His mercy is vast, that His forbearance is great, and that whoever turns to Him, He turns to him in repentance. Thus, these people, despite their lying, fabrication, wickedness, slander, disbelief, obstinacy, and what they said about the Messenger and the Qur'an, He, glorified is He, calls them to repentance and to abandoning what they are engaged in, and to Islam and guidance. As He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿Certainly, those who said, "Allah is the third of three," have disbelieved. And there is no god except one God. And if they do not desist from what they say, there will surely afflict those who disbelieve among them a painful punishment.﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 73] ﴿Will they not repent to Allah and seek His forgiveness? And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 74] And He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, those who have tormented the believing men and believing women and then have not repented will have the punishment of Hell, and for them is the punishment of the Burning.﴾ [Al-Buruj: 10] Al-Hasan al-Basri said: "Look at this generosity and bounty. They killed His allies, and He calls them to repentance and mercy."

Then He, Exalted is He, pointed to their obstinacy regarding the one to whom it was sent down, by His saying:

The discussion concerning the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[7] ﴿And they said, "What is with this Messenger that he eats food and walks in the markets? Why was an angel not sent down to him so that he might be with him as a warner?"﴾

﴿And they said, "What is with this Messenger that he eats food"﴾ meaning: just as we eat. ﴿and walks in the markets﴾ meaning: he moves about in them for his affairs, just as we walk. Al-Zamakhshari said: They mean that he should have been an angel, free from needing food and the means of subsistence; that is, his condition would differ from ours. Abu al-Su'ud said: And is it anything but due to their bewilderment (ʿamah), the feebleness of their intellects, and the shortness of their vision, which is confined to sensible things? For the distinction of the Messengers from those other than them is not by bodily matters, but by matters of the soul, as was indicated by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: I am only a human being like you, to whom it is revealed﴾ [al-Kahf: 110]. Then they descended from their demand that he be an angel to the demand that he be a human with an angel accompanying him, so that the two might support each other in warning. So they said: ﴿Why was an angel not sent down to him so that he might be with him as a warner?﴾ Then they also descended to the demand that he be given a treasure, if he was not given an angel, and they said:

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[8] ﴿Or a treasure be thrown down to him, or he have a garden from which he may eat.﴾ And the wrongdoers say, ﴿You follow none but a man bewitched.﴾

﴿Or a treasure be thrown down to him﴾, that is: from heaven, by which he would be strengthened, would have no need to seek a livelihood, and it would be a proof of his truthfulness. Then they descended and were content with proposing something easier than that, saying: ﴿Or he have a garden from which he may eat﴾ (p-4567), that is: an orchard from which he gains his sustenance. ﴿And the wrongdoers say, "You follow none but a man bewitched"﴾, that is: one whose intellect has been overcome. As for His words:

The discussion of the words of His exalted saying:

[9] ﴿Look how they have struck similitudes for you; so they have gone astray and cannot find a way.﴾

﴿Look how they have struck similitudes for you﴾ is an expression of amazement at the falsehoods which they dared to utter, and a marvelling at them. That is: look how they have said about you those sayings which lie beyond the bounds of reason. ﴿So they have gone astray and cannot find a way﴾, that is: they cannot find a way to impugn your prophethood by finding a saying upon which they can settle; or, they have gone astray from the truth, so they find no path leading to it.

Ibn Kathir said: Everyone who departs from the truth and the path of guidance is astray wherever he turns, because the truth is one, and its method is unified, its parts confirming one another.

Then, may He be exalted, drew attention to the fact that, if He willed, He would give him something better than what they propose, by His saying:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[10] ﴿Blessed is He who, if He wills, will give you better than that: gardens beneath which rivers flow, and He will give you palaces.﴾

﴿Blessed is He who, if He wills, will give you better than that: gardens beneath which rivers flow, and He will give you palaces.﴾ That is: if He wills, He will give you something better than what they said. This is that He would grant you the like of what He promised you in the Hereafter of gardens and palaces. But His wisdom decreed otherwise, so that submission would be to the truth and not to wealth, and so that it would be declared plainly that the matter is founded upon reflection and reasoning, not upon what distracts the feelings and the imagination, which is open to wrangling and disputation. Glory be to the Wise, the Exalted. And His exalted saying:

(p-4568) The discussion of His saying, may He be exalted:

[11] ﴿Nay, but they denied the Hour, and We have prepared a blazing fire for those who deny the Hour.﴾

﴿Nay, but they denied the Hour﴾ is a transitional "nay" (idrab intiqali), turning away from rebuking them by recounting their previous offense, and moving from it to rebuking them by recounting another of their offenses, in order to arrive at explaining what awaits them in the Hereafter because of it, of the various kinds of punishment, by His saying: ﴿And We have prepared a blazing fire for those who deny the Hour﴾, i.e., a fire of intense blaze (istˤar), that is, of intense kindling and flaming.

It has also been said that this "nay" is connected to what He related of them, namely: ﴿And they said, "What is this messenger?"﴾ [al-Furqan: 7], meaning: "Nay, they came with something more astonishing than all of that, namely their denial of the Hour, while the situation is that We have prepared a blaze for everyone who denies it." Indeed, their boldness in denying it, and their lack of fear of what has been prepared for those who deny it, is more astonishing than the previous statement.

It may also be connected to what follows it, as if it were said: "Nay, they denied the Hour, so how would they heed this answer? And how would they believe that God's promise of the Hereafter is hastened to you while they do not believe in it?" Then He, exalted is He, described the blaze with His saying:

The discussion of the words of His saying, may He be exalted:

[12] ﴿When it sees them from a distant place, they will hear its raging and roaring.﴾

﴿When it sees them from a distant place, they will hear its raging and roaring.﴾ That is: when it is within sight of them (i.e., close to them). The attribution of the seeing to it rather than to them is to signal that the raging and roaring come from it, due to the surging of its anger against them at the moment it sees them, either literally or figuratively. The word "from" (min) in His saying ﴿from a distant place﴾ indicates that the distance between it and them, at the time it sees them, lies beyond the normal bounds of distance in the familiar measures of separation. This adds further to the awe of its condition. Abu al-Su'ud conveyed this. "Raging" (al-taghayyuz) is the manifestation of rage (al-ghayz), which is the most intense anger, and it may be accompanied by a sound, as here. It likens the sound of its seething to the sound of one enraged and his roaring, which is a sound heard from the inside of his body, whether stated explicitly, implied metaphorically, or presented as an image.

The discussion on the interpretation of His words, may He be exalted:

[13–14] ﴿And when they are cast into it, into a narrow place, bound together, they will call out there for destruction.﴾ ﴿Do not call out today for one destruction; call out for many destructions.﴾ [Al-Furqan: 14]

﴿And when they are cast into it, into a narrow place, bound together﴾: that is, their hands are bound to their necks with chains. ﴿They will call out there for destruction﴾: that is, for ruin (halak). That is, they will call out in the manner of one who wishes for annihilation, so that they may be spared from what is worse than it. As it is said: "Worse than death is that for which death is wished."

Then it will be said to them: ﴿Do not call out today for one destruction; call out for many destructions﴾ [Al-Furqan: 14], because of the multiplicity of its successive kinds, for the punishment of Jahannam comes in varieties and manifold forms. Or its multiplicity is in terms of the renewal of its instances, even though it is one kind. Or its multiplicity is a metaphor (kinayah) for its perpetuity, because the abundant is characterized by that, as it is said in its opposite: ﴿And fruit in abundance﴾ [Al-Waqi'ah: 32], ﴿neither cut off nor forbidden﴾ [Al-Waqi'ah: 33]. It has also been said: the word "destruction" is described as "many" because of the multiplicity of the calling out or of what is called for.

[17–18] ﴿And the day He will gather them and what they worship besides Allah, and He will say, "Did you lead these, My servants, astray, or did they themselves stray from the way?" They will say, "Exalted are You! It was not for us to take any allies other than You, but You gave them and their fathers enjoyment until they forgot the remembrance, and they were a people doomed to perdition."﴾ [al-Furqan: 18].

﴿And the day He will gather them and what they worship besides Allah, and He will say﴾ — that is, Allah, exalted is He, says to the objects of worship, as a rebuke to their worshippers: ﴿"Did you lead these, My servants, astray, or did they themselves stray from the way?"﴾ — that is, from the way by their own selves, owing to their neglect of correct reflection and their turning away from the guide. ﴿They will say, "Exalted are You!"﴾ [al-Furqan: 18] — in amazement at what was said to them, because they are either angels, who are infallible, or inanimate objects that have no power over anything. Or it is a declaration of His transcendence above rivals: ﴿"It was not for us to take any allies other than You"﴾ [al-Furqan: 18] — that is, to take them as objects of worship. How could it be conceived that we would compel others to take a protector other than You? Or (min awliya') means: followers in worship. ﴿"But You gave them and their fathers enjoyment until they forgot the remembrance"﴾ [al-Furqan: 18] — this is a digression (istidrak) brought to show that they themselves were the ones who went astray, after the declaration of their own freedom from misleading them. He censured their evil conduct, in that they made the means of guidance into means of misguidance. That is: we did not lead them astray; rather, You gave them and their fathers enjoyment with various kinds of blessings, so that they would recognize its due and be thankful for it. But they plunged into desires until they forgot the remembrance — that is, Your remembrance — or the reflection upon Your blessings and the contemplation of Your signs. Thus they made the means of guidance, by their evil choice, a pretext for error — as reported by Abu al-Su'ud. ﴿"and they were a people doomed to perdition"﴾ [al-Furqan: 18] — that is, lost. The discussion of the Almighty's words:

[19] ﴿So they have indeed denied you in what you say, so you cannot avert (the punishment) nor obtain help. And whoever among you does wrong, We will make him taste a great punishment.﴾

The Interpretation of His Words, exalted is He:

[20] ﴿And We never sent before you any messengers except that they ate food and walked in the markets.﴾ That is: they were in need of nourishment through food and they moved about in the markets to earn and to trade. This does not contradict their state or their rank, for He, exalted is He, gave them good characteristics, excellent qualities, virtuous speech, complete deeds, dazzling miracles, and conclusive proofs, by which every person of intellect and every sound and upright insight can infer the truth of what they brought from God. A parallel to this noble verse is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We did not send before you any men except that We revealed to them, from among the people of the towns﴾ [Yusuf: 109], and His saying: ﴿And We did not make them bodies that do not eat food﴾ [al-Anbiya': 8].

Note (tanbih):

Al-Suyuti said in (al-Iklil): The verse permits scholars and people of righteousness to enter the markets, contrary to those who disliked it for them.

(p-4572) As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We have made some of you a trial for others. Will you be patient? And your Lord is ever Seeing.﴾ Al-Zamakhshari said: This is a consolation to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) regarding what they said and found strange of his eating food and walking in the markets, after he had argued against them with all the other messengers. The meaning is: My custom and the requirement of My wisdom is to test some of you, O people, by means of others. That is, He tested the messengers by means of those to whom they were sent, by their opposition to them with enmity, their statements that exceed the bounds of fairness, and various kinds of harm to them, and He asked them for patient endurance that is beautiful. A similar verse is His saying: ﴿You will surely hear much harm from those who were given the Scripture before you and from those who associated others with God. In His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And your Lord is ever Seeing﴾ there is additional consolation and a magnificent promise. That is: He knows what you are tested with and what others are tested with, so let not your chest be constricted. Indeed, in your patience is happiness and success in both abodes.

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[30] ﴿And the Messenger says, "My Lord, indeed my people have taken this Qur'an as something abandoned."﴾

﴿And the Messenger says﴾: that is, after witnessing their arrogance and obstinacy. ﴿"My Lord, indeed my people have taken this Qur'an as something abandoned"﴾: that is, left aside and turned away from. The clause ﴿And the Messenger says﴾ is conjoined to ﴿And those who do not expect to meet Us say﴾ [al-Furqan: 21], and what lies between them is a parenthetical digression. It was brought in to link what they said, to seek victory over them, to call down the divine relief from what they have constricted their breasts with and brought upon themselves of turbidity, and to allude to the misery of both abodes that will befall them.

Admonition:

Although the verse concerns the polytheists, and their turning away is their not believing, its noble arrangement nonetheless strikes fear into the general body of those who turn away from acting upon it and from adopting its etiquettes, which is the true meaning of abandonment. This is because people are only worshipping through it in that manner, since its recitation has no effect except upon one who reflects upon it, and none reflects upon it except one who acts by it and holds fast to its rulings.

From the benefits of the Imam Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him: his statement regarding this verse: "Abandoning the Qur'an has several kinds:

The first: abandoning hearing it, believing in it, and listening to it.

The second: abandoning acting upon it and stopping at its lawful and unlawful matters, even if one recites it and believes in it.

The third: abandoning seeking its judgment and resorting to it in the foundations of the religion and its branches, and believing that it does not yield certainty, and that its proofs are merely verbal and do not produce knowledge.

The fourth: abandoning seeking healing and remedy through it for all diseases of the hearts and their ailments, so that one seeks the cure of one's illness from other than it, and abandons seeking remedy through it."

He said: "All of this falls within this verse, although some kinds of abandonment are lighter than others." End of quotation.

In al-Iklil: "The verse contains an indication warning against abandoning the mushaf and neglecting to keep up its recitation." Likewise Abu al-Su'ud said: "In it is a hint that it is the right of the believer to be frequent in keeping up with the Qur'an, lest he fall under the apparent meaning of this noble arrangement." Then he said: "And in it is a warning that is not hidden, for the Prophets, peace be upon them, when they complained to Allah Exalted of their people, were given the punishment quickly and were not granted respite."

The Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on Surah 25, verses 32–33:

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[32–33] ﴿And those who disbelieve say, "Why was the Qur'an not sent down to him all at once?" Thus [it was revealed] that We may strengthen your heart thereby, and We have recited it in measured portions.﴾ ﴿And they do not bring you any example except that We bring you the truth and the best explanation.﴾ [al-Furqan: 33].

﴿And those who disbelieve say, "Why was the Qur'an not sent down to him all at once?"﴾ That is: in one single installment, at one single time. Glorified is He, Who has shown the falsehood of this contention and foolish objection by His words: ﴿Thus [it was revealed] that We may strengthen your heart thereby﴾, that is: We strengthen it through it to bear the burdens of the Message and to rise up to spread the truth among the leaders of ignorance. For what is sent down successively for this purpose is more stirring to resolve, firmer for determination, and more effective for the call, than its being sent down once: ﴿and We have recited it in measured portions﴾, that is: We have detailed it in a wondrous detailing, which none can match in its reach and whose limit none can attain.

Al-Qashani said: Tartil (measured recitation) is that there be placed between each portion and the next a period in which it is possible for it to take firm root in the heart, and that it become a settled disposition rather than a passing state.

﴿And they do not bring you any example﴾ [al-Furqan: 33], that is: any strange characteristic of their falsehood, whether as a slander or as a suggestion, ﴿except that We bring you the truth﴾ [al-Furqan: 33], that is: which suppresses that characteristic, as He said: ﴿Nay, We hurl the truth against falsehood, and it crushes it﴾ [al-Anbiya': 18]. ﴿And the best explanation﴾ [al-Furqan: 33], that is: clarification and guidance, out of care for you and for that for which you were sent, and abandonment of the enemies of the truth and the adversaries of right guidance.

Note:

The exegetes mention here that the verse is a refutation of the disbelievers' demand that the Qur'an be sent down all at once, as the other scriptures were sent down all at once. They hold that the view that the other scriptures were sent down in one installment is correct, and they rely on it, in the secret of the separation of the revelation from it. The fact, however, is that the claim that they were sent down in one single installment has no basis, has no trace of knowledge behind it, and is not upheld by reason. For the dispersal of revelation and the extension of its period is an established matter, necessarily so, in proportion to the length of the Prophet's stay (ﷺ). Since he was among his people, revelation necessarily came down to him in succession. Whoever examines the Torah and the Gospel that exist today will see this clearly, without doubt. The excuse of the one who holds the contrary view is his supposition that the verse alludes to the sending down of other scriptures in the same way. But not every statement is an allusion to something. The verse is rather a report of a particular proposal and an artful, obstinate stubbornness. And God knows best.

(p-4578) The discussion of the interpretation of His words, Exalted is He:

[37–39] "And the people of Noah, when they denied the Messengers, We drowned them and made them a sign for mankind, and We have prepared for the wrongdoers a painful punishment." "And ʿAd and Thamud and the people of the Rass, and generations between those many." [al-Furqan: 38] "And to each We set forth parables, and to each We destroyed with complete destruction." [al-Furqan: 39]

"And the people of Noah, when they denied the Messengers" means Noah; he is referred to in the plural as a glorification of his mission. Or it refers to him and those who preceded him, peace be upon them. "We drowned them and made them a sign for mankind, and We have prepared for the wrongdoers a painful punishment." "And ʿAd" [al-Furqan: 38] means the people of Hud. "And Thamud" [al-Furqan: 38], with or without diptotic (tanwin-less) reading: two recitations, according to the meaning of the tribe or the group. "And the people of the Rass" [al-Furqan: 38] is the name of a well. As for their prophet, it is said he was Shuʿayb, and it is said it was someone else. Some narrators here relate reports that are objectionable and not authentic, as the Hafiz Ibn Kathir, may Allah have mercy on him, has pointed out. It is therefore not permissible to be bold in relating them or to apply the verse to them, because that is "pursuing what one has no knowledge of" (qafw), and such matters are forbidden to delve into. "And generations" [al-Furqan: 38], i.e., peoples; "between those many" [al-Furqan: 38]. The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[40] ﴿And they have certainly passed by the town upon which was rained a rain of evil. Did they not see it? Rather, they did not expect resurrection.﴾

﴿And they have certainly passed by the town upon which was rained a rain of evil﴾ means: it was destroyed by stones, and these were the towns of the people of Lut (Lot). ﴿Did they not see it?﴾ means: during their passing by, looking upon the traces of God's punishment and His retribution? In this there is a rebuke for them for neglecting reflection (dhikr) when witnessing what necessitates it. ﴿Rather, they did not expect resurrection﴾ means: they were disbelievers, not anticipating any consequence or recompense.

(p-4579) The Discussion on the Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[41–42] ﴿And when they see you, they take you not except in mockery: "Is this the one whom Allah has sent as a messenger?"﴾ ﴿"He almost led us astray from our gods, had we not been steadfast in adhering to them. But they will know, when they see the punishment, who is further astray in the way."﴾ [al-Furqan: 42].

﴿And when they see you, they take you not except in mockery: "Is this the one whom Allah has sent as a messenger?"﴾ That is: they mock, saying this. The demonstrative (hadha, "this") expresses contempt, because the word "hadha" is used for that purpose. The relative pronoun's returning pronoun (ʿa'id) is omitted; the sense is "whom Allah has sent" (baʿathahu, "sent him"). And "rasulan" (as a messenger) is a circumstantial accusative (hal) from it.

﴿"He almost led us astray from our gods, had we not been steadfast in adhering to them"﴾ [al-Furqan: 42]: that is, he almost turned us away from worshipping them altogether, had we not held firm to them.

Al-Zamakhshari said: In this is evidence of the Messenger of Allah's ﷺ extreme striving in calling them, and his exerting utmost effort and obedience in winning them over, along with presenting to them the signs and miracles. To the point that, by their own claim, they were about to abandon their religion for the religion of Islam, had it not been for the extreme obstinacy and their clinging to the worship of their gods. ﴿"But they will know, when they see the punishment, who is further astray in the way."﴾ [al-Furqan: 42] is a reply from Him, Exalted, to the end of their speech. In it is a warning and an indication that they will not escape Him, however long the period of respite. The warning must befall them, so let the delay not deceive them.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[43] ﴿Have you seen him who takes his own desire as his god? Would you then be a guardian over him?﴾

﴿Have you seen him who takes his own desire as his god? Would you then be a guardian over him?﴾ This is an expression of wonder addressed to the Prophet, may the blessings of God be upon him, at the wretchedness of their condition, after the mention of their ugly sayings and deeds.

Al-Zamakhshari said: Whoever submits to desire in his religion, following it in everything he does and abandons, does not look to any proof and does not heed any evidence, is a worshipper of his desire and has made it his god. So God, exalted is He, says to His Messenger: This is one who sees no object of worship except his desire. How, then, can you call him to guidance? Would you take responsibility for him and compel him to Islam, saying, "You must submit, whether you wish or not"? But there is no compulsion in religion. Similar to this is His saying: ﴿And you are not over them a compeller﴾ [Qaf: 45] and ﴿You are not over them a controller﴾ [al-Ghashiyah: 22].

On the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[44] ﴿Or do you suppose that most of them hear or understand? They are only like livestock; rather, they are even more astray in the way.﴾

﴿Or do you suppose that most of them hear or understand? They are only like livestock; rather, they are even more astray in the way.﴾ That is: than they. For livestock direct their faculties toward seeking what benefits them and recoiling from what harms them, whereas these people have left idle their faculties, namely the intellects (ʿuqūl) by which one is guided to the truth and by which good is distinguished from evil. Then, exalted is He, pointed to some of the signs of divine unity and to the great blessings in them, which deserve to be met with gratitude rather than disbelief, as in the case of these disbelievers, through His saying, glorified is He:

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[45] ﴿Have you not considered how your Lord extends the shade? Had He willed, He would have made it still. Then We made the sun its indicator.﴾

﴿Have you not considered how your Lord extends the shade?﴾ That is: consider the wondrous artistry of it, that He made it extend and spread out so that people benefit from it. ﴿Had He willed, He would have made it still﴾ That is: fixed in its state, without extension, from length and spreading. It is from "sukna" (dwelling), or without contracting, from "sukun" (stillness), by making the sun remain in one position, so that no one would benefit from it. ﴿Then We made the sun its indicator﴾ That is: a sign by which its states are inferred in its course, regarding the shade's states: its being fixed in one place, its moving away, its widening and its contracting. Thus people build their need for the shade and their independence from it accordingly.

The Explanation of His Words, exalted is He:

[46–47] ﴿Then We draw it in toward Us, a gradual drawing in.﴾ ﴿And it is He who made the night for you as a garment, and sleep as a rest, and made the day a time of rising.﴾ [al-Furqan: 47]

﴿Then We draw it in toward Us﴾ means: We caused it to descend after We had brought it into being extended, and We erased it by the sheer power and will of Ours, at the moment the rays of the sun fall upon its place. ﴿A gradual drawing in﴾ means: at leisure, little by little, according to the rise of its indicator, along a fixed, regular pace that entails and accompanies the benefits of the creatures. In this gradual drawing in, a little after a little, there are benefits that cannot be counted or enumerated. Had it been withdrawn all at once, most of the conveniences of people would have been disrupted, both shade and sunlight alike. ﴿And it is He who made the night for you as a garment﴾ [al-Furqan: 47], meaning: a covering, like a garment. ﴿And sleep as a rest﴾ [al-Furqan: 47], meaning: a rest for the bodies, by which they make up for what they have lost of their strength. ﴿And made the day a time of rising﴾ [al-Furqan: 47], meaning: a time of dispersal in pursuit of livelihood.

The discussion of the words of His Exalted saying:

[48–49] ﴿It is He who sends the winds as heralds of good news before His mercy, and We send down from the sky pure water﴾ ﴿that We may give life thereby to a dead land and give it to drink, of that which We have created, cattle and many people.﴾ [Al-Furqan: 49].

﴿It is He who sends the winds as heralds of good news﴾: that is, spreading out the clouds. In another reading, "bushran" is read with a dammah on the "ba" in place of the "nun" and with the "shin" sukun, meaning "mubashshirat" (bearers of glad tidings). ﴿before His mercy﴾: that is, in front of the rain. This is a striking metaphor (istiʿarah). Mercy is used as a metaphor for rain, then it is made to be "rashshah" (a metaphor kept consistent with a related term). Like His saying: ﴿their Lord gives them good news of a mercy from Him﴾ [At-Tawbah: 21]. He placed it "before His hands" as a completion of it, because the bearer of good news precedes the one who receives it. It is possible that it is a figurative image (tamthiliyyah), and "bushran" is part of the completion of the metaphor, included within its whole. Whoever reads "nashran" makes it a stripping-away (tajrid) of it, because "nashr" (spreading) suits the clouds.

﴿And We send down from the sky pure water﴾: that is, purifying, in accordance with His saying: ﴿to purify you thereby﴾ [Al-Anfal: 11]. This verse is a basis for purification with water.

Al-Qadi said: Describing the water with this attribute indicates the blessing in it, and completes the favour that follows. Pure water is more wholesome and more beneficial than water mixed with something that removes its purifying quality. It also alerts that if their outward parts are to be purified, then their inward parts are more deserving of that: ﴿that We may give life thereby to a dead land﴾ [Al-Furqan: 49]: that is, by causing plants to grow. ﴿and give it to drink﴾ [Al-Furqan: 49]: that is, that water. ﴿of that which We have created, cattle and many people﴾ [Al-Furqan: 49]. Al-Karkhi said: He singled out cattle for mention, because they are our store and the foundation of the livelihood of most of the settled people. For this reason He placed their watering before the watering of people, just as He placed before it the giving of life to the earth, for it is the cause of their life and sustenance. So He placed first what is the cause of their life and livelihood.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 25, verses 50–52:

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, Exalted is He:

[50–52] ﴿And We have certainly distributed it among them that they may remember, but most of the people refused except disbelief.﴾ ﴿And had We willed, We would have sent into every town a warner.﴾ [Al-Furqan: 51] ﴿So do not obey the disbelievers, and strive against them with it, a great striving.﴾ [Al-Furqan: 52]

﴿And We have certainly distributed it﴾, meaning: We repeated this statement, which is the mention of the creation of clouds and the sending down of rain. ﴿Among them that they may remember﴾, meaning: that they may reflect, take heed, recognize the true value of the blessing in it, and give thanks. ﴿But most of the people refused except disbelief﴾, meaning: ingratitude for the blessing and denial of it. ﴿And had We willed, We would have sent into every town a warner﴾ [Al-Furqan: 51], meaning: a prophet who would warn its people, so that the burdens of prophethood would be lighter upon you. However, We did not will that, so We did not do it. Rather, We restricted the matter to you, as His words indicate, Exalted is He: ﴿That he may be a warner to the worlds﴾ [Al-Furqan: 1], out of honour and exaltation for you, and as a preference for you over the rest of the messengers.

Al-Mahayimi said: meaning, but We did not will it, because it would necessitate the division of the nations and the multiplication of disagreements. (p-4583) So We made the one a warner for all, that they might obey him or fight him. The disbelievers wish that the messengers would obey them or leave them as they are: ﴿So do not obey the disbelievers﴾ [Al-Furqan: 52], meaning: meet that with steadfastness, diligence in calling to the truth, manifesting it, firmness and patience. And do not obey them in what they want you to do. By this prohibition He intended to stir him and the believers and move them, meaning: to arouse his zeal and their zeal. Otherwise, his obeying them is not conceivable.

Abu al-Su'ud said: it is as if it were a prohibition addressed to him, upon him be blessings and peace, against conciliating them and being gentle with them. That is, because in that there would be a weakening of the truth and a veiling of it, and a prolonging of the period of its spread. Therefore He said: ﴿And strive against them with it﴾ [Al-Furqan: 52], meaning: with the Qur'an and what has been revealed to you of the truth: ﴿a great striving﴾ [Al-Furqan: 52], meaning: one not mixed with slackness, by binding them with proofs and signs, and calling them to reflect upon the various moments of existence, so that their beliefs may be shaken and their customs may appear repugnant in their eyes. This verse is among the clearest proofs of the obligation to argue against the people of falsehood, to call them to the truth with strength, and to be inventive in disputing with them with varied kinds of proofs, for the truth becomes clear through proofs, just as the months become known through the crescents.

The Interpretation of His Words, exalted is He:

[53] ﴿It is He who released the two seas, one fresh and sweet, and the other salty and bitter; and He placed between them a barrier and an impassable partition.﴾

﴿It is He who released the two seas﴾: He sent them flowing side by side, adjoining one another, such that they do not mix. ﴿One fresh and sweet﴾: that is, intensely sweet, quenching thirst. ﴿And the other salty and bitter﴾: that is, extremely salty. ﴿And He placed between them a barrier﴾: that is, a partition preventing either from mingling with the other. ﴿And an impassable partition﴾: that is, a prohibition against the effect of one of them reaching the other and mixing with it, even after one of them has entered into the other for some distance.

A subtle point:

Here al-Mahayimi (may Allah have mercy on him) takes a subtle approach in interpreting the verse, connecting its meaning to the verse before it, in a unique manner. He said (p-4584) concerning the words of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿and strive against them with it, a great striving﴾ [al-Furqan: 52]: it affects their inner selves, so that "great" surpasses what affects the outward. And if they claim: how can one strive with proofs against those who bring forth doubts that are close to them? It is said: the ultimate outcome of their matter is that they become like the two differing seas adjoining one another. Allah has removed the confusion between them after they were placed side by side, and both are perceptible; so how would the confusion not be removed between the two intelligible seas, when: ﴿It is He who released the two seas﴾, that is, placed side by side, the two between which lies the utmost difference, when: ﴿one is fresh and sweet﴾, that is, quenching thirst, and it is like the sea of proofs that yield taste, cutting off the thirst of seeking; ﴿and the other salty and bitter﴾, that is, extremely salty. It is like the sea of doubts which produce great aversion in people of taste. As for people of reflection, ﴿He placed between them a barrier﴾, that is, a preventer of mixing. It is the examination of the matters and forms of the premises, so that by this one knows the soundness of the proofs. As for the corruption of doubts, it is known through objections for which there is no answer, just as He placed between them ﴿a partition﴾ [al-Furqan: 22], that is, a prohibition against the effect of one of them reaching the other, ﴿an impassable partition﴾, that is, prevented from being prevented. And if they claim that each group sees that what it holds fast to yields taste and cuts off seeking, and that it recoils from what its opponent holds fast to even more than it recoils from bitter salt water, it is said: this is not with regard to the proofs themselves, but through the mediation of partisanship from the side of fathers, shaykhs and companions. Allah has provided an example to remove the excuse concerning this, in His words:

[Discussion on the interpretation of His words, Exalted is He:]

[54] ﴿It is He who created from water a human being, then made him a relative by lineage and by marriage. And your Lord is ever Competent.﴾

﴿It is He who created from water a human being﴾: that is, just as He brings forth the results of the sciences from their premises. ﴿Then made him﴾: that is, the human being. ﴿A relative by lineage﴾: that is, a root, a branch, or a kinsman to a people. ﴿And by marriage﴾: that is, to others, whom he defends out of loyalty to his lineage and his in-laws, so that he takes their falsehood to be truth. Likewise, the people of contention are partisan toward their fathers and their shaykhs. ﴿And your Lord is ever Competent﴾: that is, although removing this may be difficult, your Lord, who commanded you to the great struggle (jihad), is Competent to remove it, just as He was Competent in the matter of lineage and marriage. So let the believers not be concerned with either of them. End of al-Mahayimi's words, may God have mercy on him.

(p-٤٥٨٥) This is a strange line of thought in the field of allusive (ishara) interpretation, and we have cited it from him for its subtlety. As for the plain meaning of the verse, it concerns the immense power of God, glory be to Him, who created human beings and divided them from a single drop of semen into two kinds: those of lineage, meaning males to whom descent is traced, so that one says "So-and-so son of So-and-so" and "So-and-so's daughter, daughter of So-and-so"; and those of marriage, meaning females with whom one becomes related by marriage. This is clear. A parallel to it is His saying, ﴿Then He made of him two kinds, the male and the female﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 39].

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[55] ﴿And they worship, besides Allah, that which neither benefits them nor harms them, and the disbeliever is ever a helper (ẓahīr) against his Lord.﴾

﴿And they worship, besides Allah, that which neither benefits them nor harms them, and the disbeliever is ever a helper (ẓahīr) against his Lord.﴾ That is: an aide (muʿīn) to Satan in disobedience to his Lord. By "the disbeliever" is meant the category (al-jins), so this is an explicit noun in place of a pronoun, to denounce their disbelief against them, and to observe the fine closing rhymes (al-fawāṣil al-karīma).

The discussion on the interpretation (ta'wil) of His, the Exalted, saying:

[56-57] ﴿We have not sent you except as a bringer of good news and a warner.﴾ ﴿Say: "I do not ask you for any reward for it, except that whoever wills may take a path to his Lord."﴾ [al-Furqan: 57].

﴿We have not sent you except as a bringer of good news and a warner.﴾ ﴿Say: "I do not ask you for any reward for it"﴾ [al-Furqan: 57], i.e., for conveying the message, which is understood from ﴿We have sent you﴾. ﴿except that whoever wills may take a path to his Lord﴾ [al-Furqan: 57], i.e., draws near to Him through faith and obedience. That is, toward His mercy or His presence. Taking a path is meant here in its necessary meaning, because whoever travels the road to something draws near to it, indeed arrives at it.

Al-Zamakhshari said: An example is ﴿except for whoever wills﴾ [al-Furqan: 57], and what is meant is: except the act of whoever wills. The exception here is from the reward. (p-4586) It is like the words of one who has compassion for you and has striven on your behalf to obtain wealth: "I do not ask you for any reward for what you have striven, except that you preserve this wealth and do not waste it." The keeping of the wealth for yourself is not of the same kind as a reward, but he has depicted it in the form of a reward and named it by its name, and this conveys two benefits. The first: it uproots the suspicion of desire for reward from its root, as if he were saying to you: "If your keeping of your wealth is a reward, then I am seeking a reward." The second: it shows extreme compassion, and that if you preserve your wealth, he counts your preservation as a reward and is pleased with it, just as the one who is rewarded is pleased with the reward.

By my life, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was with those he was sent to in this regard and above it. End of quote.

And the exception on this view is a connected exception (istithna' muttasil) by way of claim (ida').

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[58] ﴿And put your trust in the Ever-Living who does not die, and glorify Him with His praise. And sufficient is He as one who is Acquainted with the sins of His servants.﴾

﴿And put your trust in the Ever-Living who does not die﴾, i.e., in repelling their evil and their plotting. ﴿And glorify Him with His praise, and sufficient is He as one who is Acquainted with the sins of His servants﴾, i.e., Knowing, nothing of them escapes Him, so He will recompense them for them.

The commentary on His saying, exalted is He:

[59] ﴿He who created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days, then established Himself on the Throne, the Most Merciful. So ask about Him one who is informed.﴾

﴿He who created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days﴾: i.e., of His days, exalted is He, or of the days of creation. There are two opinions among the early generations (al-salaf). ﴿Then established Himself on the Throne﴾: i.e., He rose above it with an elevation befitting His sacred majesty. Its interpretation has already been discussed. ﴿The Most Merciful﴾ is in the nominative as a laudatory epithet (madh), meaning: He is the Most Merciful. In reality it is another description of the Living (al-Hayy), as it was also read in the genitive. It was said that the relative pronoun (al-mawsul) is the subject (mubtada') and "the Most Merciful" is its predicate (khabar). It was also said that "the Most Merciful" is a substitute (badal) for the pronoun concealed in "established" (istawa).

His saying, exalted is He, ﴿So ask about Him one who is informed﴾, has several possible readings. Among them: the "bi" in "bihi" is related to (silah) "ask" (is'al). Among them also: it is related to "informed" (khabiran), and "informed" is the object (maf'ul) of "ask", meaning: ask about Him a knowledgeable man who will inform you of His mercy. Or: ask a man informed about Him and about His mercy. Accordingly, the benefit of asking about Him is that He confirms and supports its truth.

Al-Shihab said: It is also valid for the two (i.e., "ask" and "informed") to compete (tanazu') regarding the "bi". In that case there is a rare type of rhetorical ornament (badi') called al-mutajadhib (the "pulled-between"), which is when a single word lies between two clauses and can validly be made to belong to either the first or the second. Al-Sa'd mentioned it at the end of his commentary on the Miftah (Sharh al-Miftah), and this is something the authors of the badi'iyyat (works on rhetorical ornaments) overlooked. End of quote. Among them also: the "ba'" is for abstraction (tajrid), as in your saying: "I saw in him a lion," meaning: by his sight. That is: ask by his asking one who is informed, and the meaning is: if you ask Him, you will find Him informed.

In al-Kashshaf it says: This is the most appropriate reading, so that it serves as a completion (tatmim) of His saying, "He who created," and so on, for it establishes power while incorporating knowledge within it.

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[60] ﴿And when it is said to them, "Prostrate to the Most Merciful," they say, "And what is the Most Merciful? Shall we prostrate to what you command us?" And it increases them in aversion.﴾

﴿And when it is said to them, "Prostrate to the Most Merciful," they say, "And what is the Most Merciful?"﴾ That is: who is the one named by it? For they did not know Him, exalted is He, by this name, nor did they apply it to Him. Or the question is one of wonder and astonishment, as a varied form of refusal. That is: what are these names and designations you rend us with, and which strike our ears urging us to submit to them? ﴿Shall we prostrate to what you command us?﴾ "And it increases them": that is, the command to prostrate, by which is meant submission to faith, ﴿in aversion﴾: that is, arrogance toward faith.

The Explanation of His words, the Exalted:

[61] ﴿Blessed is He who placed in the sky constellations (burūj), and placed within it a lamp (sirāj) and a moon giving light.﴾

﴿Blessed is He who placed in the sky constellations (burūj)﴾ That is: stars; or they are the twelve burūj (zodiacal constellations), whose figures you see in the shapes formed by the gathering of certain stars in particular proportions, and through which the sun moves in apparent sight. ﴿And placed within it a lamp (sirāj)﴾ which is the sun. ﴿And a moon giving light﴾ That is: shining by night.

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

[62] ﴿And it is He who made the night and the day alternating succession for whoever wishes to remember or wishes gratitude.﴾

﴿And it is He who made the night and the day alternating succession﴾ i.e., following one another in succession, each of the two following the other. ﴿for whoever wishes to remember﴾ i.e., to reflect and thereby infer from this the greatness of His power. ﴿or wishes gratitude﴾ i.e., gives thanks for the blessing in both of them, through the rest (sukun) at night and the activity (tasarruf) during the day. And it is in both of them according to what they were created for.

**On the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:**

[63–64] ﴿And the servants of the Most Merciful are those who walk upon the earth in humility, and when the ignorant address them, they say, "Peace."﴾ ﴿And those who spend the night before their Lord, prostrating and standing.﴾ [al-Furqan: 64].

﴿And the servants of the Most Merciful are those who walk upon the earth in humility﴾: that is, gentle (*hayyinin*). Or, a gentle walk, meaning with tranquility and humility. They do not stamp their feet, nor do they strut out of insolence and arrogance. ﴿And when the ignorant address them, they say, "Peace."﴾ That is, when the foolish address them with harsh speech, they do not answer them in kind, but say words that contain *salam* (peace), that is, freedom from harm and sin. This is whether it takes the form of the greeting of peace, such as their saying, "Peace be upon you" (*Salamun ʿalaykum*), or other words that contain gentleness in speech, or pardon, or forgiveness, and the restraining of anger, repelling evil with what is better. (p-٤٥٨٩) ﴿And those who spend the night before their Lord, prostrating and standing﴾ [al-Furqan: 64]: that is, they have in the night the excellence of prayer and turning back to God, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿They used to sleep little of the night﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 17], ﴿and before dawn they would seek forgiveness﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 18]; and His saying: ﴿Their sides forsake their beds﴾ [al-Sajdah: 16], and the verse; and His saying: ﴿Is one who is devoutly obedient during periods of the night, prostrating and standing, fearing the Hereafter and hoping for the mercy of his Lord? Say: Are those who know equal to those who do not know?﴾ [al-Zumar: 9].

*Al-baytuta* (spending the night, *baytuta*) linguistically means entering the night. It is said: *baata yafʿalu kadha yabitu wa-yabatu*, when he does such-and-such at night. The word *baytuta* may be used figuratively for simply being in a state, but the literal meaning is more apt, due to the abundance of what has come with its meaning among what we have recited. For this reason, the *salaf* (early predecessors) said: the verse praises the night prayer and commends those who perform it. And in His saying ﴿for their Lord﴾ [al-Furqan: 64] there is an indication of sincerity in performing it and seeking His Noble Face, because that is what brings about its fruit of righteous deeds, doing good, and observing the limits of God. ﴿And standing﴾ [al-Furqan: 64]: the plural of *qaʾim* (one standing), or a verbal noun treated as such.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 25, verses 65–66:

The discussion of His saying, may He be exalted:

[65–66] ﴿And those who say, "Our Lord, avert from us the punishment of Hell; indeed, its punishment is ever-adhering destruction." Indeed, it is evil as a place of settlement and residence.﴾ [al-Furqan: 65–66].

﴿And those who say, "Our Lord, avert from us the punishment of Hell; indeed, its punishment is ever-adhering destruction."﴾ That is: perpetual destruction. What is meant by their saying this is their dread of it and their intense fear, which entails their holding fast to piety and their adherence to the strongest means. It is not merely the fluttering of the tongue without any impression upon the heart. For they only entreated the Lord and sought refuge in Him from its blaze because they knew the evil of its state. The requirement of knowing a thing is to render it its due and to act in accordance with what it necessitates. Therefore He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, it is evil as a place of settlement and residence.﴾ [al-Furqan: 66], that is: a place of settling and dwelling.

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

[67] ﴿And those who, when they spend, are neither extravagant nor stingy, but are between that, a moderate stance.﴾

﴿And those who, when they spend, are neither extravagant nor stingy, but are between that, a moderate stance.﴾ That is: they do not exceed the limit in spending, nor do they constrict themselves and their families, nor does stinginess and baseness overcome them. Rather, they were moderate in that, and the best of matters is the middle of them.

Al-Zamakhshari said: Allah described them with the moderation that lies between excess and deficiency. And the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was commanded with the like of it: ﴿Do not make your hand chained to your neck, nor extend it completely outstretched﴾ [al-Isra: 29]. Imam Ahmad narrated from Abu al-Darda', from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Part of a man's understanding (fiqh) is his gentleness in his livelihood." He also narrated from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever is moderate does not become poor." Al-Bazzar narrated from Hudhayfah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "How excellent is moderation in wealth, how excellent is moderation in poverty, and how excellent is moderation in worship."

And from al-Hasan: There is no extravagance in spending in the way of Allah. A man heard another man saying: "There is no good in extravagance." So he said: "There is no extravagance in good."

**The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:**

[68–70] ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another deity, nor kill the soul which Allah has forbidden, except by right, nor commit unlawful sexual intercourse. And whoever does that will meet a penalty.﴾ ﴿The punishment will be doubled for him on the Day of Resurrection, and he will abide therein humiliated.﴾ [al-Furqan: 69] (p-4591) ﴿Except for one who repents, believes, and does righteous work; for those, Allah will replace their evil deeds with good deeds. And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ [al-Furqan: 70].

﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another deity﴾, meaning: they do not associate anyone with their Lord in worship. So "invoking" (al-du'a') here means worship (ibadah). ﴿Nor kill the soul which Allah has forbidden﴾, meaning: He has forbidden it, in the sense that He has forbidden killing it. Among this is burying daughters alive (al-wa'd) and other things. ﴿Except by right﴾, meaning: that which removes its sanctity and inviolability. ﴿Nor commit unlawful sexual intercourse. And whoever does that﴾, meaning: whoever does what has been mentioned of these grave abominations. ﴿Will meet a penalty﴾, meaning: he will find in the Hereafter the recompense of his sin. ﴿The punishment will be doubled for him on the Day of Resurrection and he will abide therein humiliated﴾ [al-Furqan: 69], meaning: abased and despised, combining the punishment of the body and the punishment of the soul. ﴿Except for one who repents, believes, and does righteous work...﴾ [al-Furqan: 70], meaning: for whoever repents, believes, and does righteous work.

The hafiz Ibn Kathir said: In this is evidence for the validity of the repentance of the killer. There is no contradiction between this and the verse of an-Nisa': ﴿And whoever kills a believer intentionally...﴾ [an-Nisa': 93], to the end of the verse. For this verse, although it is Medinan, is unrestricted (mutlaqah), so it is to be understood as applying to one who did not repent, because that verse is restricted by repentance. Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that He be associated with﴾ [an-Nisa': 116], to the end of the verse. The authentic Sunnah has been established from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) regarding the validity of the repentance of the killer, as is mentioned as established in the story of the man who killed one hundred men and then repented, and Allah accepted his repentance, and other hadiths besides that. He then said: Regarding the meaning of His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿Allah will replace their evil deeds with good deeds﴾ [al-Furqan: 70], there are two opinions:

The first: that they replaced the place of evil deeds with the doing of good deeds. Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding this verse: They are the believers. Before their faith they were upon evil deeds, so Allah turned them away from evil deeds, transformed them toward good deeds, and substituted good deeds for evil deeds. Likewise Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: Allah substituted for them the worship of the Most Merciful in place of the worship of idols, (p-4592) and substituted for their fighting Muslims the fighting of polytheists, and substituted for their marrying polytheist women the marrying of believing women. Likewise al-Hasan said: He substituted for the evil deed the righteous deed, substituted for shirk sincerity, for debauchery chastity, and for disbelief Islam.

The second opinion: that those past evil deeds are transformed into good deeds merely by sincere repentance (tawbah nasuhah). That is only because whenever he remembers what has passed, he regrets, says "Inna lillah wa inna ilayhi raji'un," and seeks forgiveness. Thus the sin is transformed into obedience by this consideration. End of quote.

Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him, in *Tariq al-Hijratayn* has a fine exposition and a sound discussion on this point, which is not objectionable to cite, because of its great benefit.

He, may Allah have mercy on him, said (after his explanation of the hadith on Allah's rejoicing at the repentance of His servant), and its example is: Here there is an issue; this place is the most specific of contexts for explaining it. It is that the penitent, if he repents to Allah with sincere repentance, will those sins be erased and vanish, neither for him nor against him, or, when they are erased, will a good deed be recorded for him in place of each sin? This is among the matters on which people have differed, among the exegetes and others, past and present. Al-Zajjaj said: A good deed is not made in place of the sin; rather repentance is made in place of the sin, and good deeds accompany repentance. Ibn Atiyyah said: Their deeds are made, in place of their former disobediences, obedience. So that becomes a cause for Allah's mercy toward them. This was said by Ibn Abbas, Ibn Jubayr, Ibn Zayd and al-Hasan. He refuted those who said it refers to the Day of Resurrection. He said: A hadith has come in Muslim's collection through the route of Abu Dharr which indicates that Allah, glorified is He, on the Day of Resurrection, makes for whoever He wills to forgive among the monotheists, good deeds in place of his evil deeds. al-Tirmidhi and al-Tabari also mentioned it. This is the interpretation of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib regarding this verse.

Ibn Atiyyah said: And this is the meaning of the generosity of pardon. End of quote.

The mention of the hadith and the discussion about it will come later.

Al-Tha'labi said: Ibn Abbas, Ibn Jurayj, al-Dahhak and Ibn Zayd said: ﴿Allah will replace their evil deeds with good deeds﴾ [al-Furqan: 70]: Allah will replace for them the ugliness of their deeds in shirk with the fine deeds of Islam. So He replaces for them shirk with monotheism, killing believers with killing polytheists, and fornication with chastity and marriage.

(p-4593) Others said: It means Allah will replace the evil deeds they did during their state of Islam with good deeds on the Day of Resurrection. The root of the two opinions is: is this substitution in this world or on the Day of Resurrection? Whoever says it is in this world says: it is the replacement of ugly deeds and corrupt intentions with their opposites, which are good deeds, and this is a literal substitution. Those who supported this view argued that an evil deed does not become a good deed; at most its consequence is that it is erased, expiated, and its effect disappears; but that it turns into a good deed is not the case. For it was not an act of obedience, but was hateful and disliked by the Lord, so how could it turn into something beloved and pleasing?

They said: Also, what the Qur'an indicates is only the expiation of evil deeds and forgiveness of sins, as in His saying: ﴿Our Lord, forgive us our sins and expiate from us our evil deeds﴾ [Al 'Imran: 193], and His saying: ﴿And He pardons evil deeds﴾ [al-Shura: 25], and His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah forgives all sins﴾ [al-Zumar: 53]. The Qur'an is full of such. And in the Sahih, from the hadith of Qatadah on the authority of Safwan ibn Muhriz, who said: A man said to Ibn Umar: How did you hear the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) speak about the private conference (al-najwa)? He said: I heard him say: "The believer will be brought near on the Day of Resurrection to his Lord, until He places His covering (kanaf) over him, then He will make him acknowledge his sins, and He will say: Do you recognize? He will say: My Lord, I recognize. He will say: Indeed I have concealed them from you in the world, and I forgive them for you today. Then his book of good deeds will be given to him."

As for the disbelievers and hypocrites, they will be called out with them before the heads of the witnesses: "These are the ones who lied against Allah, the Mighty and Majestic."

So this hadith, which is agreed upon (muttafaq 'alayh), and which contains the care for this servant, only contains in it the covering of his sins over him in this world and their forgiveness for him on the Day of Resurrection. It does not say to him: "And I gave you a good deed for each of them." So this indicates that the ultimate outcome of evil deeds is their forgiveness and Allah's overlooking of them.

(p-4594) And Allah has said concerning the truthful: ﴿That Allah may expiate from them the worst of what they did and reward them their due for the best of what they used to do﴾ [al-Zumar: 35]. These are the best of creation. He has informed about them that He expiates for them the evil deeds of their actions and rewards them for the best of what they did. The best of what they did is only good deeds, not evil deeds, which indicates that the reward with the best is only for good deeds alone. As for evil deeds, they are nullified and their effect disappears.

They said: Also, if evil deeds themselves were transformed into good deeds with respect to the penitent, he would be in a better state than one who committed none of them, and would have more good deeds than him, because if he did evil, he shared in the good deeds he did and was distinguished from him by those evil deeds; then good deeds were turned for him, outweighing him. And how could the one with evil deeds outweigh one who has no evil deed?

They said: Also, just as when a servant does good deeds and then commits what nullifies them, they are not transformed into evil deeds for which he is punished; rather their effect is nullified and he is left neither with nor against; and his punishment is that his reward for them is not recorded. Likewise whoever does evil deeds and then repents of them, they are not transformed into good deeds. If you say: Likewise the penitent's reward is that the punishment is not recorded against his evil deeds, we do not dispute you on this. But this is not the meaning of a good deed, for a good deed requires a positive reward (thawab wujudi).

The other group, who said it is the literal substitution of the evil deed with a good deed on the Day of Resurrection, argued: The literal meaning of substitution is the establishment of a good deed in place of an evil deed. This occurs only with an actual evil deed, which has been committed and occurred. So when it is substituted with a good deed, its meaning is that it is erased and a good deed is established in its place. They said: This is why He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿Their evil deeds, good deeds﴾ [al-Furqan: 70], attributing the evil deeds to them because they engaged in them and acquired them. They said: Also, the substitution in the verse is the act of Allah and not their act, for He informed that He is the One who substitutes their evil deeds with good deeds. They said: These are, in reality, the Abdal (substitutes). For they were only called Abdal because they substituted their evil deeds with good deeds, so Allah substituted their evil deeds that they did with good deeds.

This is a ruling different from what we are discussing, for the discussion concerns the penitent from evil deeds, not one who died persisting in them without repentance. So where is the one from the other?

They said: As for what you mention, that substitution is the establishment of a good deed in place of an evil deed, that is true. And so we say: the good deed that was done has taken the place of the evil deed which, had it not been for the good deed, would have occupied its place.

They said: As for your argument from the attribution of the evil deeds to them, which indicates that they are the evil deeds that occurred, and the indefiniteness of the good deeds, which indicates that they are good deeds from Allah's grace, this is true beyond doubt. They said: As for your statement that the substitution is attributed to Allah and not to them, which indicates that it is He who substituted them from the scrolls, because they are the ones who substituted the deeds with their opposites, this is no proof for you. For Allah is the creator of (p-4596) the actions of servants. So He is the one who substitutes evil deeds with good deeds by creation and bringing into being, and they are the ones who substitute them by action and acquisition.

They said: As for your argument that recompense is of the same kind as the deed, then just as they replaced the evil of their deeds with good, God likewise replaces them in the scrolls of deeds. This is the furthest extent of the advance of the two groups and the target of the view of both parties. And to you, O fair-minded one, belongs the judgment between them. Each of them has presented his argument and established his proof, and the truth does not go beyond them or transcend them. God guides whoever helps toward guidance, so he attains the rank of those who call to God, who stand in explaining His proofs and His religion. Whoever strives toward it and wishes that no opponent oppose him and no obstacle confront him has desired the impossible for himself. So the correct position on this question, God willing, is to say: There is no doubt that the sin itself does not turn into a good deed. A good deed is an existential matter that entails reward. This is why one who abstains from what is forbidden is rewarded only for restraining his soul and withholding it from committing what is prohibited. That restraint and withholding is an existential matter, and it is the object of reward. As for one whom the sin never occurred to at all, and who never entertained it in his soul, how could he be rewarded for abandoning it? If such a person were rewarded for abandoning this sin, he would be rewarded for abandoning the sins of the scholar that never occurred to him, and these would be many times his good deeds beyond counting, since abandoning is accompanied by what is abandoned, and what is abandoned cannot be limited or measured.
