[68–70] ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another deity, nor kill the soul which Allah has forbidden, except by right, nor commit unlawful sexual intercourse. And whoever does that will meet a penalty.﴾ ﴿The punishment will be doubled for him on the Day of Resurrection, and he will abide therein humiliated.﴾ [al-Furqan: 69] (p-4591) ﴿Except for one who repents, believes, and does righteous work; for those, Allah will replace their evil deeds with good deeds. And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ [al-Furqan: 70].

﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another deity﴾, meaning: they do not associate anyone with their Lord in worship. So "invoking" (al-du'a') here means worship (ibadah). ﴿Nor kill the soul which Allah has forbidden﴾, meaning: He has forbidden it, in the sense that He has forbidden killing it. Among this is burying daughters alive (al-wa'd) and other things. ﴿Except by right﴾, meaning: that which removes its sanctity and inviolability. ﴿Nor commit unlawful sexual intercourse. And whoever does that﴾, meaning: whoever does what has been mentioned of these grave abominations. ﴿Will meet a penalty﴾, meaning: he will find in the Hereafter the recompense of his sin. ﴿The punishment will be doubled for him on the Day of Resurrection and he will abide therein humiliated﴾ [al-Furqan: 69], meaning: abased and despised, combining the punishment of the body and the punishment of the soul. ﴿Except for one who repents, believes, and does righteous work...﴾ [al-Furqan: 70], meaning: for whoever repents, believes, and does righteous work.

The hafiz Ibn Kathir said: In this is evidence for the validity of the repentance of the killer. There is no contradiction between this and the verse of an-Nisa': ﴿And whoever kills a believer intentionally...﴾ [an-Nisa': 93], to the end of the verse. For this verse, although it is Medinan, is unrestricted (mutlaqah), so it is to be understood as applying to one who did not repent, because that verse is restricted by repentance. Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that He be associated with﴾ [an-Nisa': 116], to the end of the verse. The authentic Sunnah has been established from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) regarding the validity of the repentance of the killer, as is mentioned as established in the story of the man who killed one hundred men and then repented, and Allah accepted his repentance, and other hadiths besides that. He then said: Regarding the meaning of His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿Allah will replace their evil deeds with good deeds﴾ [al-Furqan: 70], there are two opinions:

The first: that they replaced the place of evil deeds with the doing of good deeds. Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding this verse: They are the believers. Before their faith they were upon evil deeds, so Allah turned them away from evil deeds, transformed them toward good deeds, and substituted good deeds for evil deeds. Likewise Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: Allah substituted for them the worship of the Most Merciful in place of the worship of idols, (p-4592) and substituted for their fighting Muslims the fighting of polytheists, and substituted for their marrying polytheist women the marrying of believing women. Likewise al-Hasan said: He substituted for the evil deed the righteous deed, substituted for shirk sincerity, for debauchery chastity, and for disbelief Islam.

The second opinion: that those past evil deeds are transformed into good deeds merely by sincere repentance (tawbah nasuhah). That is only because whenever he remembers what has passed, he regrets, says "Inna lillah wa inna ilayhi raji'un," and seeks forgiveness. Thus the sin is transformed into obedience by this consideration. End of quote.

Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him, in *Tariq al-Hijratayn* has a fine exposition and a sound discussion on this point, which is not objectionable to cite, because of its great benefit.

He, may Allah have mercy on him, said (after his explanation of the hadith on Allah's rejoicing at the repentance of His servant), and its example is: Here there is an issue; this place is the most specific of contexts for explaining it. It is that the penitent, if he repents to Allah with sincere repentance, will those sins be erased and vanish, neither for him nor against him, or, when they are erased, will a good deed be recorded for him in place of each sin? This is among the matters on which people have differed, among the exegetes and others, past and present. Al-Zajjaj said: A good deed is not made in place of the sin; rather repentance is made in place of the sin, and good deeds accompany repentance. Ibn Atiyyah said: Their deeds are made, in place of their former disobediences, obedience. So that becomes a cause for Allah's mercy toward them. This was said by Ibn Abbas, Ibn Jubayr, Ibn Zayd and al-Hasan. He refuted those who said it refers to the Day of Resurrection. He said: A hadith has come in Muslim's collection through the route of Abu Dharr which indicates that Allah, glorified is He, on the Day of Resurrection, makes for whoever He wills to forgive among the monotheists, good deeds in place of his evil deeds. al-Tirmidhi and al-Tabari also mentioned it. This is the interpretation of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib regarding this verse.

Ibn Atiyyah said: And this is the meaning of the generosity of pardon. End of quote.

The mention of the hadith and the discussion about it will come later.

Al-Tha'labi said: Ibn Abbas, Ibn Jurayj, al-Dahhak and Ibn Zayd said: ﴿Allah will replace their evil deeds with good deeds﴾ [al-Furqan: 70]: Allah will replace for them the ugliness of their deeds in shirk with the fine deeds of Islam. So He replaces for them shirk with monotheism, killing believers with killing polytheists, and fornication with chastity and marriage.

(p-4593) Others said: It means Allah will replace the evil deeds they did during their state of Islam with good deeds on the Day of Resurrection. The root of the two opinions is: is this substitution in this world or on the Day of Resurrection? Whoever says it is in this world says: it is the replacement of ugly deeds and corrupt intentions with their opposites, which are good deeds, and this is a literal substitution. Those who supported this view argued that an evil deed does not become a good deed; at most its consequence is that it is erased, expiated, and its effect disappears; but that it turns into a good deed is not the case. For it was not an act of obedience, but was hateful and disliked by the Lord, so how could it turn into something beloved and pleasing?

They said: Also, what the Qur'an indicates is only the expiation of evil deeds and forgiveness of sins, as in His saying: ﴿Our Lord, forgive us our sins and expiate from us our evil deeds﴾ [Al 'Imran: 193], and His saying: ﴿And He pardons evil deeds﴾ [al-Shura: 25], and His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah forgives all sins﴾ [al-Zumar: 53]. The Qur'an is full of such. And in the Sahih, from the hadith of Qatadah on the authority of Safwan ibn Muhriz, who said: A man said to Ibn Umar: How did you hear the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) speak about the private conference (al-najwa)? He said: I heard him say: "The believer will be brought near on the Day of Resurrection to his Lord, until He places His covering (kanaf) over him, then He will make him acknowledge his sins, and He will say: Do you recognize? He will say: My Lord, I recognize. He will say: Indeed I have concealed them from you in the world, and I forgive them for you today. Then his book of good deeds will be given to him."

As for the disbelievers and hypocrites, they will be called out with them before the heads of the witnesses: "These are the ones who lied against Allah, the Mighty and Majestic."

So this hadith, which is agreed upon (muttafaq 'alayh), and which contains the care for this servant, only contains in it the covering of his sins over him in this world and their forgiveness for him on the Day of Resurrection. It does not say to him: "And I gave you a good deed for each of them." So this indicates that the ultimate outcome of evil deeds is their forgiveness and Allah's overlooking of them.

(p-4594) And Allah has said concerning the truthful: ﴿That Allah may expiate from them the worst of what they did and reward them their due for the best of what they used to do﴾ [al-Zumar: 35]. These are the best of creation. He has informed about them that He expiates for them the evil deeds of their actions and rewards them for the best of what they did. The best of what they did is only good deeds, not evil deeds, which indicates that the reward with the best is only for good deeds alone. As for evil deeds, they are nullified and their effect disappears.

They said: Also, if evil deeds themselves were transformed into good deeds with respect to the penitent, he would be in a better state than one who committed none of them, and would have more good deeds than him, because if he did evil, he shared in the good deeds he did and was distinguished from him by those evil deeds; then good deeds were turned for him, outweighing him. And how could the one with evil deeds outweigh one who has no evil deed?

They said: Also, just as when a servant does good deeds and then commits what nullifies them, they are not transformed into evil deeds for which he is punished; rather their effect is nullified and he is left neither with nor against; and his punishment is that his reward for them is not recorded. Likewise whoever does evil deeds and then repents of them, they are not transformed into good deeds. If you say: Likewise the penitent's reward is that the punishment is not recorded against his evil deeds, we do not dispute you on this. But this is not the meaning of a good deed, for a good deed requires a positive reward (thawab wujudi).

The other group, who said it is the literal substitution of the evil deed with a good deed on the Day of Resurrection, argued: The literal meaning of substitution is the establishment of a good deed in place of an evil deed. This occurs only with an actual evil deed, which has been committed and occurred. So when it is substituted with a good deed, its meaning is that it is erased and a good deed is established in its place. They said: This is why He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿Their evil deeds, good deeds﴾ [al-Furqan: 70], attributing the evil deeds to them because they engaged in them and acquired them. And He made the good deeds indefinite and did not attribute them to them, because they are not from their making or acquisition, but are purely Allah's grace and generosity.

They said: Also, the substitution in the verse is the act of Allah and not their act, for He informed that He is the One who substitutes their evil deeds with good deeds. If what you mention were intended, He would have attributed the substitution to them, for they are the ones who substitute their evil deeds with good deeds, and deeds are attributed to their doer and acquirer, as He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿So those who did wrong substituted a word other than that which had been said to them﴾ [al-Baqarah: 59]. As for what comes from other than the doer, He attributes it to His own substitution, as He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿And We substituted for them their two gardens with two gardens﴾ [Saba': 16]. So when He, glorified is He, informed that it is He who substitutes their evil deeds with good deeds, this indicates that it is a thing He Himself did to their evil deeds, not that they did it of their own accord (p-4595), though its cause is from them, namely repentance, faith and righteous deeds.

They said: This is indicated by what Muslim narrated in his Sahih from Abu Dharr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I know the last of the people of Paradise to enter Paradise, and the last of the people of the Fire to leave it. A man will be brought on the Day of Resurrection, and it will be said: Present to him his minor sins, and lift from him his major ones. So his minor sins will be presented to him, and it will be said: You did on such and such a day such and such, and on such and such a day such and such. He will say: Yes. He cannot deny, while he is apprehensive about his major sins being presented to him. Then it will be said to him: Indeed, for you there is a good deed in place of every evil deed."

They said: These are, in reality, the Abdal (substitutes). For they were only called Abdal because they substituted their evil deeds with good deeds, so Allah substituted their evil deeds that they did with good deeds.

They said: Also, the recompense is of the same kind as the deed. Just as they substituted their evil deeds with good deeds, Allah substituted them, from the scrolls of the recording angels, with good deeds as a fitting recompense.

The first group said: How can you argue with the hadith of Abu Dharr in support of your view, when it is explicit that this man whose evil deeds were substituted with good deeds was punished for them in the Fire, to the point that he was the last of its people to leave it? So he was punished for his evil deeds, and their effect disappeared through punishment, and so a good deed was substituted for each of them. This is a ruling different from what we are discussing, for the discussion concerns the penitent from evil deeds, not one who died persisting in them without repentance. So where is the one from the other?

They said: As for what you mention, that substitution is the establishment of a good deed in place of an evil deed, that is true. And so we say: the good deed that was done has taken the place of the evil deed which, had it not been for the good deed, would have occupied its place.

They said: As for your argument from the attribution of the evil deeds to them, which indicates that they are the evil deeds that occurred, and the indefiniteness of the good deeds, which indicates that they are good deeds from Allah's grace, this is true beyond doubt. But from where does it follow that Allah's grace is with them, accompanying their acquisition of them by His grace?

They said: As for your statement that the substitution is attributed to Allah and not to them, which indicates that it is He who substituted them from the scrolls, because they are the ones who substituted the deeds with their opposites, this is no proof for you. For Allah is the creator of (p-4596) the actions of servants. So He is the one who substitutes evil deeds with good deeds by creation and bringing into being, and they are the ones who substitute them by action and acquisition.

They said: As for your argument that recompense is of the same kind as the deed, then just as they replaced the evil of their deeds with good, God likewise replaces them in the scrolls of deeds. This is true, and we say it too. The evil deeds that were prepared and destined to appear in the scrolls were replaced with good deeds placed in their stead. This is the furthest extent of the advance of the two groups and the target of the view of both parties. And to you, O fair-minded one, belongs the judgment between them. Each of them has presented his argument and established his proof, and the truth does not go beyond them or transcend them. God guides whoever helps toward guidance, so he attains the rank of those who call to God, who stand in explaining His proofs and His religion. Or He excuses a seeker who travels alone on the path of his quest, whose hope of a companion on the way has been cut off. The utmost of his wish is that he be left free to continue his journey and that his path not be cut off. Whoever is shown such a banner and does not strive toward it has been content with the inferior and has obtained the bargain of the defrauded. Whoever strives toward it and wishes that no opponent oppose him and no obstacle confront him has desired the impossible for himself. Even if he is patient with its hardship and severity, he is, by God, the clear triumph and the abundant portion. My success is only by God; in Him I place my trust and to Him I turn in repentance.

So the correct position on this question, God willing, is to say: There is no doubt that the sin itself does not turn into a good deed. A good deed is an existential matter that entails reward. This is why one who abstains from what is forbidden is rewarded only for restraining his soul and withholding it from committing what is prohibited. That restraint and withholding is an existential matter, and it is the object of reward. As for one whom the sin never occurred to at all, and who never entertained it in his soul, how could he be rewarded for abandoning it? If such a person were rewarded for abandoning this sin, he would be rewarded for abandoning the sins of the scholar that never occurred to him, and these would be many times his good deeds beyond counting, since abandoning is accompanied by what is abandoned, and what is abandoned cannot be limited or measured. Would he be rewarded for all of that? This is not conceivable. And if a good deed must be an existential matter, then the penitent who repents of the sins he committed has, with each sin, accompanied it by regret for it, restraint of his soul from it, and resolve not to return to it. These are good deeds beyond doubt. Repentance has erased the trace of the sin and has left behind this regret and resolve, which is a good deed, and that evil deed has been replaced by a good deed. This is the meaning of the saying of some commentators (p-٤٥٩٧): "Repentance is placed in the stead of the evil deed, and the good deed along with repentance." When each of his evil deeds has been repented of, his repentance from it is a good deed that has taken its place. This is the meaning of the replacement, not that the evil deed itself is transformed into a good deed.

Some commentators said regarding this verse: He gives them, through regret for every evil they committed, a good deed. In light of this, by God's praise the difficulty has been removed, the correct position has become clear, and it has become evident that each of the two groups did not depart from the requirement of knowledge and proof.

As for the hadith of Abu Dhar, although the replacement in it applies to the persistent sinner who was punished for his evil deeds, it indicates by a stronger inference the occurrence of replacement for the penitent who has desisted and regrets his evil deeds. For the sins for which the persistent sinner was punished, when He removed their trace through punishment, they remained as though they had never been. God gave him in place of each of those evil deeds a good deed, because what befell him on the Day of Resurrection of excessive regret over them, along with the punishment, does not entail the removal of their trace and their transformation into good deeds. The removal of their trace through sincere repentance is greater than the removal of their trace through punishment. So if they are replaced with good deeds after their removal through punishment, it is all the more fitting and more worthy that they be replaced with good deeds after their removal through repentance. The effect of repentance in this erasure and replacement is stronger than the effect of punishment, because repentance is a voluntary act performed by the servant willingly, out of love for God and awe of Him. As for punishment, its expiation is of the same kind as the afflictions that befall him not by his choice, rather God does it. And there is no doubt that the effect of voluntary acts which God loves and is pleased with, in erasing sins, is greater than the effect of the afflictions that reach him without his choice.

The end of his words, may God have mercy on him. And His saying, exalted is He:

The Discussion on the Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[71] ﴿And whoever repents and does righteous deeds, then indeed he turns back to Allah with a [sincere] turning back.﴾

﴿And whoever repents and does righteous deeds, then indeed he turns back to Allah with a [sincere] turning back.﴾ That is: whoever abandons sins, feels remorse for them, and enters upon righteous deeds, then by this he has turned back (tā'ib) to Allah with a turning back (matāb) that is pleasing to Him, expiating sins and securing reward. Al-Zamakhshari affirmed this.

The verse is clear that righteous deeds, and persevering in them in speech and action, are a condition for the validity and acceptance of repentance, and that repentance is of no account without righteous deeds. Let whoever imagines that repentance is merely seeking forgiveness with the tongue, or humbling oneself with the limbs, without any righteous deed that pleases the Most Merciful, take heed of the meaning of this verse.

The discussion of His saying, Exalted is He:

[72–73] ﴿And those who do not bear false witness, and when they pass by idle talk, they pass by with dignity.﴾ ﴿And those who, when they are reminded of the signs of their Lord, do not fall down before them deaf and blind.﴾ [Al-Furqan: 73]

﴿And those who do not bear false witness﴾ means: those who do not attend falsehood. One says "shahida kadha" (he witnessed such-and-such), meaning he attended it. So "al-zur" (falsehood) is the object, with an omitted noun before it, meaning: its places. "Yashhadun" is from "al-shahada" (witnessing). "Al-zur" is in the accusative either as a verbal noun (masdar) or by removal of the preposition, meaning: "shahadat al-zur" (the testimony of falsehood) or "bi-l-zur" (with falsehood). Al-Zamakhshari pointed to both possibilities in his words: "It may be that they shun the gatherings of liars and the sessions of sinners, so they do not attend them nor draw near to them, out of aloofness from mixing with evil and its people, and in order to safeguard their religion from what would damage it, because witnessing falsehood is a form of participation in it. For this reason it was said of those who look on at everything that the Sharia has not permitted: 'They are partners in the agency of the sin,' because their presence and their gaze are evidence of approval of it, a cause of its existence, and an increase in it, since what was empowered over its doing is the admiration of the spectators and their desire to look at it. It may also be that they do not give false testimony," and that is the end of the quotation. False testimony is deliberately lying against another.

Al-Mubarrad said in "al-Kamil": It is related from Ibn Abbas regarding this verse, ﴿And those who do not bear false witness﴾, that he said: "The festivals of the polytheists." Ibn Mas'ud said: "Al-zur is singing." It was said to Ibn Abbas: "Is this not also included in bearing false witness?" He said: "No. The verse about false witness is: ﴿And do not pursue that of which you have no knowledge. Indeed, the hearing, the sight, and the heart — about all of these one will be questioned.﴾" [Al-Isra: 36]

﴿And when they pass by idle talk, they pass by with dignity﴾ means: it happens that they pass by people of idle talk, and idle talk is everything that is base and to be discarded. They pass by turning away from them, honouring themselves by not engaging in discourse with them, as in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And when they hear idle talk, they turn away from it and say, "For us are our deeds, and for you are your deeds. Peace be upon you. We do not seek the ignorant."﴾ [Al-Qasas: 55]. This includes overlooking indecencies, pardoning sins, and using euphemism for what is repugnant to state plainly. This is because "kiraman" is the plural of "karim" in the sense of one who honours himself and others by forgiveness and the like.

﴿And those who, when they are reminded of the signs of their Lord﴾ [Al-Furqan: 73], meaning: when they are admonished by them and warned.

﴿Do not fall down before them deaf and blind﴾ [Al-Furqan: 73], meaning: rather they fall upon them, hearing with attentive ears and gazing at them with seeing eyes. (p-4599) The expression was framed by negating the opposite, as an allusion to what the disbelievers and hypocrites do of intense turning away, refusal, and aversion; the falling down in that state is used as a striking metaphor for it. This is because of their reduction from humanity to the level of beasts, or even lower than that, since beasts hear and see, and we have negated these from them.

The Noble Revelation contains many descriptions of the believers, of the trembling of their hearts at the remembrance of Him, Exalted is He, and of the increase of their faith when the Wise Reminder is recited to them. For this reason Qatada said of them: "They are a people who understood Allah and benefited from what they heard of His Book." May Allah have mercy on al-Hasan al-Basri, for he said: "How many a man recites it and falls down upon it, deaf and blind."

The Interpretation of His Words, exalted is He:

﴿And those who say, "Our Lord, grant us from among our spouses and offspring comfort of the eyes, and make us leaders for the righteous."﴾ [74].

﴿And those who say, "Our Lord, grant us from among our spouses and offspring comfort of the eyes"﴾ i.e., children and grandchildren, by whom the eyes are comforted and the souls are gladdened by their presence, because of their possession of virtues and their characterization by the best of qualities. The "comfort of the eye" (qurrat al-'ayn) is either from qarr, meaning coldness, because the tear of joy is cold, which is why its opposite is said: "May God make his eye hot" (asKhana Allahu 'aynahu); or from qarar (settledness), because the eye does not look at anything else. It is also permitted that "min" (from) be explanatory (bayaniyya), and on this is the view of many that it contains a supplication for the righteousness of spouses. As for His words, exalted is He, ﴿and make us leaders for the righteous﴾, i.e., imams (leaders), He used the singular for its indication of the genus, while observing the rhyme (fawasil). That is: we are to be followed in good; or guides and callers to good, for that is greater in reward and better in final return. Al-Qastallani said in "al-Iklil": the verse contains a request for leadership in good. And in "al-'Aja'ib" by al-Kirmani: al-Qaffal and other exegetes said: the verse is evidence that seeking leadership in religion is obligatory. End of quote.

Likewise al-Zamakhshari said, citing some of them: indeed it contains what indicates that leadership in religion must be sought and desired. And His words, exalted is He:

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 25, verses 75–77:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

﴿Those will be rewarded with the high chamber for what they endured, and they will be received therein with greetings and peace,﴾ ﴿abiding therein; excellent is it as a place of settling and dwelling.﴾ [al-Furqan: 76] ﴿Say: "My Lord would not care for you were it not for your supplication. But you have denied, so it will be inevitable."﴾ [al-Furqan: 77] [75–77].

﴿Those﴾ is a demonstrative referring to those characterized by what has been mentioned. It is either a predicate for "the servants of the Most Merciful," or a subject whose predicate is: ﴿will be rewarded with the high chamber for what they endured﴾, meaning: for enduring the hardships of striving (mujahadat) in calling to good deeds, persevering in good deeds, and avoiding what is forbidden. Al-ghurfah (the high chamber) is the highest rank of dwellings in Paradise. ﴿And they will be received therein with greetings and peace﴾, meaning: the angels will greet them and salute them. Or some of them will greet others and salute them. The intent is that they will receive therein honor and reverence; for them is peace, and upon them is peace. ﴿Abiding therein; excellent is it as a place of settling and dwelling﴾ [al-Furqan: 76] because its people are safe from calamities, and they abide forever and ever.

Then he pointed out how it is possible, or conceivable, that He would care for them, when there has occurred from them what contradicts it, by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿But you have denied﴾ [al-Furqan: 77], meaning: you denied what the truth had come to you with. That is: the custom of those who denied and persisted has already been recited to you: ﴿so it will be inevitable﴾ [al-Furqan: 77]. Al-lizam (inevitability) is a verbal noun interpreted as an active participle, used for emphasis. That is: this news, or this wise Reminder, or this great matter, the matter of the Message, will be enduring and established. It opens from the truth a gate, and people enter the religion of God in multitudes. God has indeed fulfilled His promise, aided His servant, honored His soldiers, and defeated the confederates alone. We ask Him, exalted is He, for the best of what is with Him.

This part was completed, by the praise of God, exalted is He, on Saturday morning, on the 8th of Safar al-Khayr, at the threshold of the Sananiyya Mosque in Damascus, in the year 1325, by the hand of its poor compiler Muhammad Jamal al-Din ibn Muhammad Sa'id ibn Qasim ibn Salih al-Qasimi al-Dimashqi, may his Master pardon him. Amin.
